current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: The Duane total cross section of the six principal light-ion reactions, with the coefficients the 2019 NRL Plasma Formulary tabulates on page 44. Its energy argument is the incident-ion energy with the target at rest, which is the frame the fit was made in.

The record evaluating that fit at the equivalent stationary-target energy rather than at the declared beam energy, and carrying both. Under the equal-mass kinematics the configuration uses, a colliding-beam machine reaches the centre-of-mass energy of a stationary-target machine at four times its own beam energy; the ratio is exact and asserted as an equality.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: A body set that depends on the configuration: a beam-target device is a beam pipe, a solid target and the dump behind it; a colliding-beam device is two beam pipes and nothing between them. Its beams are each other's target and they meet in vacuum, so neither an interaction region nor the beam itself carries a body.
Both directions of that rule refused rather than defaulted: a beam-target device given no target assembly, and a colliding-beam device given one.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

description: Validated frozen declaration objects (ClockModel, DiagnosticChannelPlan, DeferredCandidate, DiagnosticPlan) rejecting catalogue misalignment: inapplicable candidates, inadmissible carriers, evidence-vocabulary mismatches, incompatible clock kinds, Nyquist violations, unresolvable event-timing bounds, and incomplete candidate coverage — every rejection branch is tested.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Bank normalisation and fill state (bank.py; Lee eqs. 4–6, 9, 43): E0, t0, Z0, I0, the quarter period, delta, ln c, La, beta, and the ideal-gas fill. Anchors: the E0 and trise columns of Table 1 for PF1000, NX3, INTI and PF400J within 2.5 % and 2 % (the table's own rounding; the sub-kilojoule row prints one significant digit).

Axial characteristics (axial.py; eqs. 5–7, eq. 1 at rest): the transit time, alpha, the characteristic speed and the terminal snowplow speed at a declared current. Anchor: the terminal speed at the peak current against the peak va column of the four rows within 15 %; it overestimates every row by 7–14 % and the tests assert that sign, so the deviation is evidence, not noise. Both direct public implementations reject equal/reversed electrodes and require the exact bank-derived logarithm. Finite-input overflow/underflow, every invalid scalar and composed-record propagation are exercised through the actual Python, Rust and PyO3 entry points; representable adjacent radii remain accepted. See the input/native contract.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Device geometry (DeviceGeometry): nine SI parameters of the mechanical envelope (insulator-sleeve length and wall, cathode rod radius and cathode length, chamber bore, wall and length, back-wall and end-wall thickness) plus the integer rod count, with fail-closed positivity, the rule that at least three rods are declared, the axial rule that the cathode fits the chamber length, canonical bytes, a SHA-256 digest and a strict parser refusing unknown fields, non-finite literals and a non-integer rod count; every rejection branch is tested. The anode radius, the cathode radius and the anode length stay in the configuration's ElectrodeSet. The layout is the qualitative Mather-type arrangement of the documents already on file for the level-0 models (IAEA-TECDOC-1829; S. Lee, J. Fusion Energ. 33 (2014) 319). The reference fixtures are synthetic; one anchor fixture carries the dimensions IAEA-TECDOC-1829 p. 231 prints for the NX3 assembly A20Z160 (anode radius 20 mm and length 160 mm, twelve rods of 12 mm diameter on a circle of radius 51 mm, insulator-sleeve length 30 mm) and a test proves the model reproduces every one of them. Reproducing a printed dimension is an anchor, never a claim about that machine.

Kernel library pin: the manifest block kernel_library lists the four geometry kernels, the placement kernel and the numerics kernel at one commit and inventory digest; the contract test proves the manifest, the pyproject.toml dependency, the Rust crate revision, the lock file, the installed library version and the CI install steps name one commit.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: Same design, same bodies: the eighteen B-rep bodies of the reference design (anode, insulator sleeve, twelve cathode rods, chamber wall, two closing walls, pinch column) are built at the names, roles, material tokens and extents of the tier-G1 model, proven by an inventory comparison against build_device_model.

The cathode is a cage at this tier too: one solid per rod, named in ring order, each centred on the configuration's cathode circle at the centre the tier-G1 model uses (agreement to 1e-12), each of the declared rod radius and spanning the declared cathode length. The centres are the library's, so the two tiers cannot drift apart.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description:
Radial pressure balance across the separatrix. The plasma pressure at the field null carries the whole external magnetic pressure, p_max = B_e^2 / 2 mu0; averaging the balance over the separatrix cross-section introduces the average-beta relation = 1 - x_s^2 / 2 and gives

and, with a declared particle density, the summed electron and ion temperature.

The empirical kinetic-scale bound. S = r_s / delta_i with the ion skin depth delta_i = c / omega_pi, the elongation E = l_s / (2 r_s), their ratio, and whether the ratio sits below the bound 3.5 printed by Bala et al. (arXiv:2204.07978v1, equation 14). A test drives two configurations that differ only in separatrix length across the bound and proves the verdict turns there.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: The separatrix as its own published shape, not a column: r(z) = a sqrt(1 - |z / b|^m) from Ma et al. (arXiv:2103.00839v1, equation 13). The poles are exactly zero and the midplane is exactly (0, a), both asserted; the profile increases strictly in z; and an even sample count is refused because it would leave the widest point of the body off the model.

The ellipse reproduces its own closed form. At m = 2 the body is an ellipsoid of revolution; the sampled volume rises monotonically towards 4/3 pi a^2 b and is within 1e-5 of it at 801 samples. The bound is measured, not assumed: convergence is not clean second order because the ellipse meets the axis with infinite slope, and the measured deficits are 3.1e-2, 6.5e-4 and 8.3e-6 at 11, 81 and 801 samples. A larger shape index gives a fuller body, which is what "racetrack-like" means in the source.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The same five bodies as exact solids of revolution, each checked fail-closed by the library's evidence kernel: volume and area against their analytic closed forms within the measure tolerance, the faceted volume within the chord-deficit bound, and the faceted volume against the tier-G1 mesh of the same design within the polygon-deficit bound.
The separatrix needs no new closed form: a pole contributes no end disc, so its area reference is the lateral sum alone and its volume reference the same frustum sum tier G1 uses.

current_surfaces.name: Device configuration
description: Validated frozen parameter objects (SubcriticalBlanket, NeutronSource, DeviceConfiguration) rejecting non-finite values, non-positive extents, an unknown fertile class, and any multiplication factor outside the strictly subcritical interval (0, 1) — the hard invariant of a driven hybrid blanket — with every rejection branch tested.

The subcritical multiplication M = 1 / (1 - k_eff) (cf. Bethe, Phys. Today 32 (1979) 44) as a documented derived quantity, with an advisory finding for k_eff > 0.98 (inside the documented margin to criticality), reported and never clamped.

description: The nullable timing_uncertainty_s member, declared null on every channel because no event-relative candidate is applicable here; a non-null value is refused. This keeps the channel shape identical across the portfolio under envelope 1.1.0.

Validated frozen declaration objects (ClockModel, DiagnosticChannelPlan, DeferredCandidate, DiagnosticPlan) rejecting catalogue misalignment: inapplicable candidates, inadmissible carriers, evidence-vocabulary mismatches, incompatible clock kinds, and incomplete candidate coverage — every rejection branch is tested.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: The four published figures of merit of a fusion-fission hybrid: the thermal power ratio (equation 1), the hybrid electrical efficiency (equation 2), the off-line and on-line capacity ratios (equations 6 and 7), and the number of fission reactors supported (equation 4).

Their agreement where the source states one: equation 7 against the form of equation 5, over a sweep of driver and blanket values. The agreement is asserted within a relative tolerance and not as an equality, because measurement over 6372 parameter points showed 317 of them disagreeing in the last places — the two forms group the same factors differently, and floating-point multiplication is not associative.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Eight bodies in a fixed order — the plasma column and one per material zone of the radial build — each a cylinder or an annular tube about z from the shared kernel library.

The anchor, twice over. Table C1 of the filed report prints both the zone thicknesses and the outer radii they produce. The geometry is declared from the thicknesses alone, so all eight printed outer radii are computed; every one comes back as the same IEEE double, asserted as an equality with no tolerance. The stronger form of the same check reads the outermost vertex of each built body back out and recovers the same eight radii from the tessellation itself.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The same eight bodies as exact B-rep solids through the shared library's cad group, each checked fail-closed by the library's evidence kernel against its analytic closed forms and against its tier-G1 twin, and exported as normalised STEP bytes with a digest.

Which deflection binds, measured for this family rather than copied. At the declared 1e-4 m and 0.02 rad the angular criterion binds: the eight bodies span radii from one metre to two and a third and every deficit agrees to about seven significant figures.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: The three printed diameters nest. The cryostat's outer limiter diameter (1.140 m), the charging station's (1.157 m) and the charging coil's bore (1.300 m) are printed in three different places and must be consistent for the machine to be assemblable. The test asserts the nesting and the 17 mm and 80 mm clearances it implies, and a separate test asserts that a floating coil too large for the bore is refused, so the nesting is a gate rather than a remark.

The four declared dimensions each carry their reading. The two sub-coil outer diameters make the pack continuous, and the gaps they produce are asserted to be exactly zero while remaining reported and never gated; the cryostat height is asserted equal to half the difference of its two printed diameters, the circular-cross-section reading of the word "toroidal"; the levitation coil height is asserted equal to the sum of the printed plate, sheet and tape thicknesses.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The faceting fraction is a range and not a number. The bound falls as a body's inner radius grows while the mesher's deviation does not, so the widest-bore body sits at more than twice the fraction of the narrowest. The test asserts the whole range and asserts that the ratio between the extremes exceeds two, so a future change that flattened the spread would be noticed.

The mesh-difference check is tight. Because the tier-G1 deficit equals the polygon bound rather than sitting under it, the margin of that check is exactly the faceting deficit. A test asserts that the margin equals the faceting deficit to five per cent, which is the statement that the check has no hidden slack.

inputs: Pulse timing/clock, FRC/liner inputs, triggering/state/drive variables, reset and quantisation contracts.

Initial phases in radians, axial positions in metres, velocities in metres per second, integration step/time horizon, phase/spatial lock tolerances and the sampled safety envelope accompany the bank specification, initial voltage and requested compression pulse.

Recovery requires both its coil/load specification and an expansion trajectory: time, radius, radial velocity, magnetic field and field rate. The simple MIF decision consumes those supplied channels; it does not evolve the self-consistent compression physics itself.

The inspected full-chain diagnostic generates a deterministic ADC-reference stream, preserves address/polarity/clock/sequence meaning and projects admitted events into a separately bound CONTROL exact-current path. Its calibration statement is a normalised simulation profile, not a calibrated facility measurement.

The full-chain entry point selects actual MIF/CONTROL/FUSION/NeuroCore source checkouts, requires the selected Rust stochastic backend and builds the tracked trigger fabric with Verilator. Source availability and installed dependency/tool compatibility must be checked in the actual run.
outputs: Qualified model trajectories, trigger/runtime records and actual maintained counterpart outputs.

The simple entry point returns fire, abort unsafe, hold no lock or abort bank infeasible, plus reasons, lock time, kinematic/merge traces, a sampled safety certificate, bank feasibility/energy and optional prescribed-trajectory recovery. These are model outputs, not a physical trigger or measured energy recovery.

When run successfully, the full-chain demonstration records MIF decisions, the CONTROL permit and scheduler, diagnostic event provenance and actual local RTL cycles. It requires exactly one nominal RTL pulse before calling the FUSION model; the injected unsafe case must suppress the pulse and avoid that model call.

The admitted model call produces radius, radial velocity, magnetic-field and time channels. The field-rate channel is explicitly derived with numpy.gradient, then used for Faraday recovery; the runtime checks flux-budget diagnostics. This remains a source-described software-model output with its own physics evidence requirements.

A stateful diagnostic result carries canonical event/address-map/projection/control-execution identities and ingress telemetry. Its actuation_authority field is false; it does not replace the stateless permit, scheduler or independent veto.

The documented bundle contains nominal.json, safety_veto.json, fusion_trajectory.npz, summary.md and chain_manifest.json. The runtime reruns both cases and compares canonical payloads and trajectory channels before writing provenance/artifact digests. A separate timing package keeps cycle proofs, post-route reports and calibrated end-to-end measurements in distinct classes.
acceptance: A sampled envelope certificate, literature-described merge kinematics or supplied expansion is not a full plant safety case, experimentally calibrated phase law or complete three-dimensional reactor design.

The described causal chain runs software and local RTL simulation. Hardware waveform equivalence, post-route timing, calibrated end-to-end operation and a physical trigger path retain separate requirements.

current_surfaces.name: Device configuration
description: Validated frozen parameter objects (MaterialLiner, MagnetisedTarget, DeviceConfiguration) rejecting non-finite values, non-positive extents, an unknown liner class, and a missing target premagnetisation (the defining property of magneto-inertial fusion) — every rejection branch is tested.

The specific-kinetic-energy relation e = v^2 / 2 as a documented derived quantity, with an advisory finding for implosion velocities beyond the slow material-liner regime ~30 km/s (LINUS-class studies; Moses, Krakowski & Miller, LA-7686-MS, 1979), reported and never clamped.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: Diagnostic and clock declarations
description: Validated frozen declaration objects (ClockModel, DiagnosticChannelPlan, DeferredCandidate, DiagnosticPlan) rejecting catalogue misalignment: inapplicable candidates, inadmissible carriers, evidence-vocabulary mismatches, incompatible clock kinds, Nyquist violations, unresolvable event-timing bounds, and incomplete candidate coverage — every rejection branch is tested.

current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Shell mechanics. The mass of the annular liner as the exact annulus rho pi ((r + d)^2 - r^2) l, not the thin-shell approximation: the two differ by d / (2 r + d), which is 0.74 % at the filed design point and comparable to the tolerance the energy anchor is asserted at, so discarding it would eat most of that margin. A test asserts the difference is exactly that fraction. From the mass follow the kinetic energy at the declared velocity, the drive pressure B^2 / 2 mu0 of the target's initial field, and the characteristic time r_0 / v, which the record names as a scale rather than a trajectory.

Flux compression B(r) = B_0 (r_0 / r)^2 and adiabatic compression T(r) = T_0 (r_0 / r)^(2 (gamma - 1)). Both are conservation laws in their ideal limit and both are recorded as upper bounds: a real liner has finite conductivity and loses flux, a real compression radiates and conducts. The non-integer power goes through the shared library's deterministic kernel rather than the platform's, and a test asserts the two are the same call.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Five bodies in a fixed order, each closed and outward-oriented: the target plasma in the bore, the liner shell, the coaxial return conductor and the two end electrodes. The bodies nest the way the current path does, the electrodes meet the liner exactly at its ends, and each electrode spans the full outer radius — a feed narrower than the return path would not close the circuit.

Every derived radius is the previous one plus a declared thickness, and the accessors validate the bore they are handed rather than trusting it. Every envelope field is refused when zero, negative, infinite or not-a-number, and the parser refuses an unknown key, a missing field and a value of the wrong type, booleans included.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The same five bodies as exact solids, each checked fail-closed by the library's evidence kernel: volume and area against their analytic closed forms within the measure tolerance, the faceted volume within the chord-deficit bound, and the faceted volume against the tier-G1 mesh of the same design within the polygon-deficit bound.
Every body is a cylinder or an annular tube, so each has a well-defined smallest circular radius and the deficit bound needs no special case here.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: The three stages, expressed mechanically. The azimuthal field the axial current puts at the liner surface, mu0 I / 2 pi r, and its magnetic pressure; the liner's mass, measured from the outside in because that is how this family declares a liner, and its implosion kinetic energy at a declared velocity; and the preheat energy deposited divided by the fuel volume the bore encloses. The field is checked to fall as one over the radius, not merely to be computed.

Stagnation. Axial flux conservation B_z (r_0/r)^2 and adiabatic compression (r_0/r)^(2(gamma-1)), both ideal limits recorded as upper bounds. The non-integer power goes through the shared library's deterministic kernel and a test asserts the two are the same call.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Five bodies in a fixed order, one per stage of the family: the fuel column, the liner shell, the laser entrance window and the Helmholtz-like coil pair. The fuel sits in the bore, the coils clear the liner, the window caps the bore at one end only, and the pair is symmetric about the midplane.

The Helmholtz ratio is reported, never imposed. The source says Helmholtz-like; the anchor declares a pair at the condition and a test asserts the ratio is exactly one, while the synthetic reference sits away from it and is accepted. Turning a qualified word into an invariant would invent a constraint the source did not state.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The same five bodies as exact solids, each checked fail-closed by the library's evidence kernel against its analytic closed forms, its chord deficit bound and its tier-G1 twin. Every body is a cylinder or a tube, so each has a well-defined smallest circular radius.

The deflection is set from the scale of this family, not copied. A MagLIF bore is two millimetres where the liner family's is two hundred and the deficit bound is 2 d / r, so the liner family's 1e-4 would make the guarantee ten per cent here. This tier declares 1e-5 and a test asserts every body's bound stays under two per cent.

description: Validated frozen parameter objects (JetArray, DeviceConfiguration) rejecting non-finite values, non-positive extents, and a single-jet declaration (a converging liner needs multiple jets) — every rejection branch is tested.

The standard-mechanics kinetic-energy relations (per jet and total) as documented derived quantities, with an advisory finding for arrays below the documented spherically convergent size ~30 jets (Hsu et al., IEEE Trans. Plasma Sci. 40 (2012) 1287), reported and never clamped.

current_surfaces.name: Diagnostic and clock declarations
description: Validated frozen declaration objects (ClockModel, DiagnosticChannelPlan, DeferredCandidate, DiagnosticPlan) rejecting catalogue misalignment: inapplicable candidates, inadmissible carriers, evidence-vocabulary mismatches, incompatible clock kinds, Nyquist violations, unresolvable event-timing bounds, and incomplete candidate coverage — every rejection branch is tested.

A data-only pin (ObservabilityBinding) to the SPO observability-profile catalogue release 1.0.0 (d70c0de696534e5a77066ef8420cf7ca17bc4d7321984b0ac83523dbc1dce609), bound in turn to reactor registry 1.0.0; a plan pinned to any other release is rejected.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: The array as a forming liner. Its mass and kinetic energy in SI; the half-angle one jet subtends at the centre; the fraction of the sphere the caps add up to, checked monotone in both the count and the jet radius; the shell density of the liner the jets are meant to form; and its ram pressure.

A spherical convergence, not a cylindrical one. The density gain is the volume ratio (r_0/r)^3 and the temperature gain (r_0/r)^(3(gamma-1)). At gamma = 5/3 that exponent is exactly 2.0 in binary, which was measured: the cylindrical families' 2(gamma-1) is 1.3333333333333335 and is not exactly four thirds, so the equality is written here and could not be written there. The non-integer power goes through the shared library's deterministic kernel.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

description: The nullable timing_uncertainty_s member, declared null on every channel because no event-relative candidate is applicable here; a non-null value is refused. This keeps the channel shape identical across the portfolio under envelope 1.1.0.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Numerics substrate (numerics.py): the natural logarithm, the exponential and the real power are the pinned shared kernel library's (scpn-reactor-kernels, kernel numerics_transcendental; commit and inventory digest in reactor-domain.json, kernel_library); tests prove each wrapper returns the library value bit for bit and re-raises the library's domain refusal as NumericsError (a configuration error). The manifest block is validated field by field and a contract test proves the manifest, the pyproject.toml dependency, the installed library version, rust/Cargo.toml, rust/Cargo.lock and the CI install steps name one commit.

Mirror ratio and loss boundary (mirror.py; Endrizzi eq. 3.6, Frank eqs. 2.3–2.5): R_m = R_vac / sqrt(1 - beta) with beta refused outside [0, 1); the loss boundary sin^2 theta = (1 + q Delta phi / E) / R_m for ions and electrons, with the electrons fully confined below e Delta phi (the source: "only electrons with energies above 5 T_e leave") and a cone at or beyond unity reported as "no trapped region"; at zero potential the isotropic fraction equals the configuration's loss_cone_fraction() bit for bit. The typography of the printed eq. 2.5b is resolved by the source's own statement (ADR 0005 item 3).
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Device geometry (DeviceGeometry): thirteen SI parameters of the axisymmetric mirror envelope (central-cell vessel bore and wall; central-cell coil offset, bore, winding and length; mirror-coil warm bore, winding and length; expansion-tank bore, wall and length; end-wall thickness) with fail-closed positivity on every field, canonical bytes, SHA-256 digest and a strict parser refusing unknown fields, non-numbers and non-finite literals; every rejection branch is tested. Two envelope relations are refused in the direction they are wrong: a central-cell coil inside the vessel wall it is wound around, and a tank no wider than the throat it opens from. The mirror-coil positions are not repeated here: each coil is centred on a throat at ±central_cell_length_m / 2, read from the validated configuration.

Declared axial field profile (scpn_mirror_core.geometry.profile): the profile contract (at least two (z, B) samples, pairs, finite heights, strictly positive fields, strictly increasing heights) with the offending index named; the midplane sample at z = 0 required because the declared midplane radius belongs to that plane; the throat field as the maximum; and the single relation r(z) = r_mid sqrt(B_mid / B(z)) checked sample by sample against an independent evaluation, with the midplane radius reproduced bit for bit and the narrowest radius equal to r_mid / sqrt(R_m) for the mirror ratio the configuration validates.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: Same design, two tiers: the CAD bodies carry the same names, roles, materials and order as the tier-G1 bodies, and the CAD record carries the identical declared field profile, flux-tube profile and aperture clearances as the tier-G1 record — so the two tiers are one design, not two similar ones.

B-rep against the closed forms: every body's volume and surface area from the pinned OpenCASCADE kernel against the analytic closed form within the library's declared relative tolerance 1e-9. For the flux tube that closed form is the exact frustum-stack sum of its linear profile, so the comparison is an agreement between two exact quantities, not a convergence.

inputs: Complete published kernel source, representation/domain, deterministic operation graph, shape/units and precision.
A kernel needs finite, in-range values under its cited equation or standard method and validity domain. Refusal preserves unsupported input rather than clamping it into a result.
Selected geometry/CAD operations retain their own units and analytic references. The source distinguishes metre-based STEP/B-rep data and explicit unit conversion before volume meshing.
Consumer manifests must identify distribution, version and inventory digest. A family name alone cannot select a reproducible kernel implementation.
outputs: Versioned public kernels, exact inventory/build identities, native counterparts and consumer pin proofs.
The source requires Python-floor and selected Rust operation-order/bit-pattern correspondence for mathematical kernels, with separate evidence per kernel.

The source supplies distinct representations: a canonical closed triangle mesh and digest, binary STL, glTF 2.0 binary with metadata, optional B-rep/STEP and a tetrahedral MSH volume mesh. Native units, placement, precision and backend identity stay explicit. Export bytes and canonical mesh identity are different records; none supplies an accepted reactor-physics result.
Inventory entries retain identifiers, module/source, maturity, parity and benchmark/evidence pointers. Consumer pins remain independent records.
acceptance: Kernel manifest (kernels-domain.json) with validator; generated kernel inventory with drift check; workflow modularity guard; preflight.

Geometry kernels (landed 2026-09-02) — vendored deterministic unit circle (polynomial sine and cosine with exact octant symmetry), the closed-mesh contract (TriangleMesh: closure and orientation validation, signed volume, surface area, canonical bytes, SHA-256), solid-cylinder and annular-tube tessellation, binary STL and glTF 2.0 binary exports of any body list, native kernels bit-exact with the Python floor, and a standard-conformant benchmark; computational_prototype (ADR 0002, VALIDATION.md#geometry-kernels). Origin: moved from SCPN-Z-PINCH-CORE (its copies are retired once it pins this library).

Placement kernel (landed 2026-09-03) — exact translation of a vertex stream, the centres of identical bodies equally spaced on a circle around the axis, and their neighbour separation, so a device can carry a part that is not axisymmetric (a squirrel-cage cathode, a ring of feed conductors) without re-implementing geometry; the unit circle is generalised to any point count of at least three while keeping the tessellation counts bit-identical, and both are mirrored natively and measured in the geometry benchmark; computational_prototype (ADR 0007, VALIDATION.md#geometry-kernels).

Axial profile kernel (landed 2026-09-03) — bodies whose radius varies along the axis: a closed solid and a closed tube through a sampled (z, radius) profile, linear between samples and interpolating nothing beyond that, with the exact frustum-stack volume and lateral area. A constant-radius profile reproduces the existing primitives vertex for vertex, so the generalisation moves no pinned digest; the tessellation deficit against the closed form is exactly the polygon deficit of the segment count. Mirrored natively with bit-pattern parity and measured in the geometry benchmark; computational_prototype (ADR 0010, VALIDATION.md#geometry-kernels). Relaxed state (relaxation.py; eqs. 4–5): the reversal threshold Theta_rev = j_{0,1} / 2 = 1.2024... is the model's own identity and the configuration's advisory 1.2 is proven to be its rounding; F_bfm(Theta_rev) = 0 exactly in double arithmetic; F_bfm -> 1 as Theta -> 0 with a deviation bounded by Theta^2 at four decades; F_bfm is positive below the threshold, negative above it and decreasing towards the pole; the reversal radius exists exactly when Theta > Theta_rev and tends to a at the threshold; the product identity B0 J1(2 Theta) = <B_phi> Theta holds to 1e-15 relative; the model refuses Theta <= 0 and Theta >= j_{1,1} / 2 with the stated reason; the edge-field advisory reproduces the configuration's current cross-check.

No dimension of any device is used.

Anchor: the geometry tier carries a second fixture pair built from the values that source prints — the aspect ratio R/a = 5 of its single helical eigenstates (Fig. 1, 3 and 8) and the reversal parameter F = -0.05 it calls the shallow reversed case. That source works throughout in units normalised to the plasma minor radius and prints no length in metres, so the anchored quantities are dimensionless; the absolute radii that realise the ratio, the pinch parameter, the field amplitude, the operational limits and every envelope thickness are declared and said to be declared. Both tiers are checked against it: the tessellated plasma column and the B-rep solid each return the printed ratio from their own bounding box, the tessellated one exactly. Reproducing a printed value is an anchor, never a claim about a machine.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Sharp-boundary state (balance.py): beta = p / (B^2 / 2 mu0) from the configuration, the equal-species ion temperature T = p / (2 n e), the Alfvén speed B / sqrt(mu0 n m_i) and the end-to-centre propagation time (L/2) / v_A at a declared density and ion mass; beta = 1 (allowed by the configuration) is refused by every sharp-boundary model, never clamped. Tests verify the closed forms and the m_i^-1/2, n^-1/2 scalings.

Scyllac l = 1, 0 toroidal equilibrium (toroidal_equilibrium.py; source p. 2, eqs. 3 and 7): the excursions delta_1, delta_0, their product against the required -2 / ((3 - 2 beta) h^2 a R), the balance ratio (unity at equilibrium, tested to 1e-12), the required field-ratio product and the auxiliary field ratio of eq. (3). Anchor: the 5-m sector point of Fig. 2 (beta 0.85, a 0.7 cm, R 2.375 m, h 0.19 /cm) yields a required product of −0.0059 against the measured −0.0064 and the plotted sharp-boundary value ≈ −0.0065; the quotient forms of the excursions are the ones that reproduce it, which resolves the scan's typographical ambiguity, with a declared 10 % tolerance.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Device geometry (DeviceGeometry): seven SI parameters of the linear theta-pinch envelope (discharge-tube bore and wall, tube overhang, main coil wall, mirror-coil length and wall, end-flange thickness) with fail-closed positivity, canonical bytes, SHA-256 digest and a strict parser refusing unknown fields and non-finite literals; every rejection branch is tested. The coil bore radius and the coil length are not repeated here: they are the validated configuration's coil_radius_m and coil_length_m. The layout is the qualitative arrangement of the linear theta pinch described in section VI.A (pp. 13-14) of the Scyllac review already on file for the level-0 models (W. E. Quinn et al., LA-UR-73-1053 (1973)): a straight theta pinch whose main compression coil is flanked by mirror coils of their own bank, main and mirror coils sharing one bore, with a discharge tube of smaller bore inside them. The reference fixtures are synthetic; one anchor fixture carries the printed dimensions (coil bore 11 cm, coil length five metres, mirror-coil length 16 cm, tube bore 8.8 cm) and a test proves the model reproduces every one of them. Reproducing a printed dimension is an anchor, never a claim about that machine.

Kernel library pin: the manifest block kernel_library is validated field by field (distribution, version, 40-hex source commit, 64-hex inventory digest, sorted unique kernel identifiers, no other field); a contract test proves the manifest, the pyproject.toml dependency, the installed library version and the CI install steps name one commit.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: Same design, same bodies: the seven B-rep bodies are built at the names, roles, material tokens and extents of the tier-G1 model, proven by an inventory comparison against build_device_model.

B-rep measures against the analytic closed forms: every body's OpenCASCADE volume and surface area agree with the analytic cylinder or tube forms within the library's measure tolerance 1e-9 relative (measured 0 to 4.9e-16 for volume and 0 to 1.7e-16 for area in the reference environment), fail-closed by construction of the record. The closed forms the comparison uses are evaluated on the fixture values in the library's operation order, not written as decimal literals: the axial extents are sums of three fixture values whose binary result is not the decimal one, and an equality against a literal would be a false precision.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Three closed forms nothing in the repository owned yet. The plasma volume by Pappus's theorem, exact for the elliptic cross-section; the vacuum toroidal field at the inboard and outboard edges and their ratio, with the ordering inboard > axis > outboard asserted; and the normalised plasma current I_p / (a B_t).

Composition, not restatement. The Greenwald limit and the cylindrical safety factor stay on OperationalLimits; a test asserts the record's values are exactly what those methods return, so there is one source of truth per number and no room for two implementations to drift apart.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Three bodies of the cylindrical periodic equivalent in a fixed order — plasma column, vacuum vessel, toroidal-field winding — each a cylinder or an annular tube about z from the shared kernel library, over the periodic length 2 pi R0.

The cross-capability identity. The built column's volume divided by the volume the physics record computes by Pappus's theorem is the inscribed-polygon ratio (n / 2 pi) sin(2 pi / n) and nothing else, at 8, 64 and 256 segments and in both anchored regimes. The column is built at the area-equivalent radius a sqrt(kappa) precisely so that this holds. Asserted within a relative tolerance rather than as an equality: measured, the two sides part by 3 units in the last place at 8 segments and 133 at 256, which is 3e-14 relative.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: The same three bodies as exact B-rep solids through the shared library's cad group, each checked fail-closed by the library's evidence kernel against its analytic closed forms and against its tier-G1 twin, and exported as normalised STEP bytes with a digest.

Which deflection binds, measured rather than copied. On a device metres across it is the angular criterion that sets the tessellation, not the linear one. Three measurements say so: across a tenfold change in the linear deflection the relative deficit did not move at all; halving the angular deflection quartered it; and the deficit is the same for all three bodies and both regimes although their radii differ by tens of per cent and a factor of nearly two.

description: Validated frozen declaration objects (ClockModel, DiagnosticChannelPlan, DeferredCandidate, DiagnosticPlan) rejecting catalogue misalignment: inapplicable candidates, inadmissible carriers, evidence-vocabulary mismatches, incompatible clock kinds, Nyquist violations, unresolvable event-timing bounds, and incomplete candidate coverage — every rejection branch is tested.

A data-only pin (ObservabilityBinding) to the SPO observability-profile catalogue release 1.0.0 (d70c0de696534e5a77066ef8420cf7ca17bc4d7321984b0ac83523dbc1dce609), bound in turn to reactor registry 1.0.0; a plan pinned to any other release is rejected.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: Level-0 device physics
description: Bennett equilibrium (Bennett, Phys. Rev. 45 (1934) 890; Haines, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 53 (2011) 093001, §2): the integral pressure balance, the Bennett density and pressure profiles, the azimuthal field of that profile, the enclosed current, and the Alfvén speed and transit time at the on-axis density. Tests close the pressure balance to machine precision, integrate the profile back to the line density, verify Ampère's law at sampled radii, and check the I^2, 1/N and m_i^{-1/2} scalings.

Ideal-MHD stability estimates (Haines 2011 §5; Kadomtsev, Reviews of Plasma Physics 2 (1966) 153): the order-of-magnitude growth rate gamma ~ k v_A for a declared wavenumber and the Kadomtsev m=0 criterion -d ln p / d ln r < 4 gamma_ad / (2 + gamma_ad beta) on the Bennett profile in closed form. Tests reproduce the published conclusion that the Bennett profile is sausage-unstable at every radius for gamma_ad = 5/3 and that the reduced criterion flips exactly at gamma_ad = 2.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: 3D geometry
description: Device geometry (DeviceGeometry): eight SI parameters of the coaxial envelope (inner electrode, outer electrode bore and wall, acceleration and assembly regions, chamber bore and wall, end walls) with fail-closed positivity and containment invariants, canonical bytes, SHA-256 digest and a strict parser refusing unknown fields and non-finite literals; every rejection branch is tested. The layout is the qualitative coaxial-gun/assembly-region arrangement of the sheared-flow z-pinch literature (Shumlak et al., Phys. Plasmas 24 (2017) 055702); no dimension of any device is used.

Kernel library pin: the manifest block kernel_library is validated field by field (distribution, version, 40-hex source commit, 64-hex inventory digest, sorted unique kernel identifiers, no other field); a contract test proves the manifest, the pyproject.toml dependency, the installed library version and the CI install steps name one commit.
current_surfaces.verification_basis: Declared evidence in the project source; project checks were not rerun for this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: CAD geometry and export
description: Same design, same bodies: the six B-rep bodies are built at the names, roles, material tokens and extents of the tier-G1 model, proven by an inventory comparison against build_device_model.

B-rep measures against the analytic closed forms: every body's OpenCASCADE volume and surface area agree with the analytic cylinder or tube forms within the library's measure tolerance 1e-9 relative (measured 0 to 1.8e-15 in the reference environment), fail-closed by construction of the record.

scope: the analytic device physics models: closed-form and 0-D models from the z-pinch literature evaluated on the validated configuration (no solver code, no FUSION seam);

the device geometry and its 3D model: the coaxial mechanical envelope (electrodes, acceleration and assembly regions, chamber, end walls) and the deterministic analytic-surface model derived from it, with open-format exports, plus the tier-G2 B-rep CAD model of the same bodies with a normalised deterministic STEP export (no engineering property carried); the tessellation, mesh, export and CAD kernels themselves are the shared kernel library's, pinned here, not owned here;

the device boundary: plant and experiment truth, shot lifecycle, and configuration policy for linear plasma columns confined by the azimuthal magnetic field of their own axial current, including the classical equilibrium (Bennett-type pressure balance), the dominant sausage/kink instability structure, and sheared-axial-flow stabilisation as the family's second registry configuration;
pulsed-power driver semantics at device level (capacitor banks, pulse lines, electrode assemblies) as configuration facets;
diagnostic semantics, reference frames, and clock identity declarations;
actuator-response model boundaries and the declared safety envelope;
the device-owned CONTROL adapter specification;
the binding to the SCPN Phase Orchestrator reactor registry (version 1.0.0, digest 786d9542ce76c56dd7748fa948b17efed6c073525e527ce90e6d5e29a2d00090);
the machine-readable domain manifest reactor-domain.json and the derived Studio portfolio descriptor (integration state not_federated).

no parameter set describes or validates any real machine

dossier.critical_boundary: Static balance/shear criteria cannot prove dynamic stability, sustained confinement or gain; source support and wall/end-loss scope explicit.

Earlier technical-guide captures retain their dates. Published source checkpoint on 1 November 2026: f10db9c175f05461ad622b606d3e8d0b83ada3cf. Selected source fingerprints and available reading documents were reconciled to this public revision; older technical captures retain their dates. No new runtime, scientific or physical acceptance is inferred. PyPI sc-neurocore 4.0.0 was observed on 1 November 2026 with non-yanked published files. This package observation does not qualify component extraction, hosted CI, installed consumers or hardware. The separate sc-neurocore-engine publisher also reports 4.0.0. Benchmark figures and the 26 March MNIST run retain their original scope and date.

dossier.purpose: Permanent public development, composition and integration workbench for stochastic and spiking neural modelling, encoding, learning, simulation, selected hardware compilation and evidence inspection.

current_surfaces.name: Public stochastic-neuron, bitstream arithmetic, equation-neuron and equation-to-Verilog workflows
current_surfaces.maturity: documented supported base-package scope, locally source-inspected; not rerun or physical qualification in this dossier
current_surfaces.evidence: Dated architect source inspection, 13 October 2026; no independent execution or physical acceptance by this atlas.

current_surfaces.name: Optional Rust engine, Studio and source-checkout research/polyglot/hardware flows
current_surfaces.maturity: profile-specific mixed maturity; source presence and README declarations are not whole fidelity/physical acceptance
current_surfaces.evidence: Dated architect source inspection, 13 October 2026; no independent execution or physical acceptance by this atlas.
description: Current source scope; expected outputs and acceptance requirements are separate.

expected_outputs.deliverable: Complete parent catalogue/Studio/retained component fidelity and stable supported interfaces; permanent coherent workbench composition of independently owned components.
expected_outputs.acceptance: Original roadmap whole gates, model source fidelity separate from cross-runtime parity, installed consumer/native/RTL and physical evidence within their respective exact scopes.
expected_outputs.qualification_requirements: Original roadmap whole gates, model source fidelity separate from cross-runtime parity, installed consumer/native/RTL and physical evidence within their respective exact scopes.

inputs: Model equations and parameters with model-specific units; input signals/event streams; topology/state/seed/time-step; explicit runtime/compile/target profile.
Input values can enter an encoder as probabilities and become binary or packed bitstreams. The model must preserve the chosen unipolar/bipolar arithmetic and encoding meaning.
The documented network path combines populations, projection weights, stimuli and per-timestep neuron state. Learning and optional synchronisation have their own execution-path scope.
Selected hardware workflows start from equations or an imported network and retain weights, delays, thresholds, hierarchy and precision through graph lowering and emission.
outputs: Spike/state simulations, bitstream computations, selected generated fixed-point Verilog, composed workflow/evidence views and scoped source-bound benchmark artefacts.
The documented simulation spine produces spikes, membrane voltages, firing rates and packed bitstreams, followed by analysis, decoding or export.

NIR graph interchange and selected .v/.sv generation connect software models to compilation. HDL bundles, formal collateral, synthesis/placement records and target decks retain the selected workflow’s scope.

The permanent parent workbench brings model, data, learning, silicon and evidence responsibilities together. The named focused repositories are a roadmap of responsibilities, not independent release proof.
acceptance: Original roadmap whole gates, model source fidelity separate from cross-runtime parity, installed consumer/native/RTL and physical evidence within their respective exact scopes.
The canonical map keeps source-only research and non-package contributed work outside its supported binary surface. They must not become production capabilities through the portfolio map.
The document distinguishes Python network features from Rust/MPI subsets and canonical SC dispatch from independent polyglot kernels. Broad backend lists cannot establish full feature parity.
The hardware pipeline describes traceability, formal and caller-supplied safety evidence. Its library tooling does not provide certification or approval of a deployed product.

Software-runtime parity, scientific source-model fidelity, Python/RTL agreement, synthesis/timing and measured hardware behaviour need their own evidence. Base-package generated RTL and a complete polyglot row cannot stand in for all of those results.

The published equation-native-IR documentation checked on 28 October 2026 describes compile_to_ir for supported EquationNeuron models and recompile_ir for exact canonical graph replay. It requires a matching engine build; supported source guards, word widths, integration/pipeline modes and simulation-only trap checks retain explicit limits. inputs: Hash-bound run manifests and raw event/cycle data; selected plant/controller/load/fault/profile inputs; for neural use, independently owned wrapper, identified stimuli and bounded step/state/service mapping.

CONTROL records sample readiness/read, timely and late actuator commands, deadlines, safe state and faults. COMPUTE has input/start/done/output/interrupt events. Each run binds the actual event-domain snapshot, profile and cycle identity; a timestamp is meaningful within that declared timebase.

Placement, controller coefficients, mechanical/thermal fixed-point plant, sample period, warm-up, load and fault schedule belong to the run. Native or ISA execution in simulated transactions still declares rtl_simulation; host monotonic timestamps do not become fabric ticks.

The host needs complete 16-byte little-endian records, source/build artefacts, manifest hashes and final coherent loss/status information before reset. A completion receipt cannot fill missing events or repair an invalid run.

Driver/BSP revision, rail/shunt mappings, units, sample configuration and per-read host/fabric brackets accompany PAC1934 acquisition. Its raw journal is distinct from a qualified power series; no physical acquisition or aligned energy result is established here.
outputs: Simulation-provenance reports and raw timing/coverage/gap observations; target future board latency/jitter/deadline/fault and rail-energy distributions with admitted instrument/uncertainty.

Event bytes, optional tracking/power series and a versioned manifest retain the exact run-domain, configuration and referenced artefacts. Actual native source/context bindings belong to the original acquisition. This explanation creates no new run package.

Scheduling is SAMPLE_READ minus SAMPLE_READY; compute is ACT_WRITE minus SAMPLE_READ; loop latency is ACT_WRITE minus SAMPLE_READY. Reports retain sample counts, duration, distributions and deadline/fault response. Missing observations remain visible.

Adjacent-cycle jitter uses the absolute change in the same complete post-warm-up interval, without bridging gaps; peak-to-peak spread is separate. Tracking RMS/peak describes observed samples when declared, with expected/observed/missing coverage and an invalid partial run.

Energy is averaged over many cycles and reported per rail and together, not per core or as an atomic per-cycle rail snapshot. JSON/CSV/SVG reports retain simulation or unverified board-declaration scope; a valid file structure cannot supply independent board acceptance.

Overflow remains invalid even if capture later recovers. Saturated drop counters are lower bounds; missing records cannot establish an absent actuator write or reconstruct an interval. Reset flushes the run, so status custody precedes reset.
acceptance: Actual licensed target build/CDC/timing, known-period/delay/overflow/instrument acceptance, complete source-bound repeated board runs; simulated ticks remain simulation.

Implemented source and described simulations do not qualify physical clocks, CDC, processor placements, I/O, control quality or power. architecture_only is the source qualification state, while development is actively in progress.
Nonzero overflow invalidates the run; saturating counts are lower bounds and drain frequency alone cannot establish throughput. Completion receipts do not reconstruct missing event pairs.

Sequential rail reads do not share an exact instant, and the core rail supplies both processors and fabric. Power units, window timing and calibration need qualification; energy per cycle is a window mean rather than an atomic per-cycle/per-core observation.

The cited architecture reading retains its earlier date; newly selected document/code readings carry current byte fingerprints. The evolving neural document is an uncommitted source observation pending owner acceptance. No instrument, neural experiment, benchmark, proof or hardware run was executed for this update.

inputs: Whole classified parent source and existing consumers, explicit supported numerical/data/resource contracts; final per-component units and stable version matrix require owner freeze.
A population supplies a model class or registered name, neuron count and explicit parameters. Distinct population objects retain distinct state even when their configurations match.
Projection CSR arrays, source/target populations, weights and delays determine how events become currents. Uniform and per-synapse delay storage are different contracts.
Duration, timestep, stimuli, monitors and optional plasticity determine the reference simulation. Backend selection must preserve those semantics and the population configuration.
outputs: Versioned numerical kernel API and a coherent base simulation profile.
Spike monitors retain neuron/timestep events; state and rate monitors provide selected traces and binned firing rates. These observations describe the configured simulation.

Population stepping, readable state, reset and externally supplied voltages have explicit roles. Matching a class name does not establish that a backend transports every configured or already-evolved state.
Fixed-point widths, fractional scaling, thresholds, reset and refractory conventions must be selected together when comparing Python, native and RTL forms.
acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.

Current Rust admission accounts for Python-only dynamics and population construction/state divergences. Forced Rust refuses incompatible semantics; automatic selection uses the Python path when the Rust admission conditions fail.
The documented native FixedPointLif accepts signed int16 state with data_width 1–16 and a valid fractional range. A wider Python configuration does not establish native support.
The documented LIF exporter produces arrays and fixed-point parameters, omits connectivity, and retains its own coverage limitations. Read the separate compiler path for a different emission scope.

Selected trained weights are normalised per layer for SC probabilities, with optional declared export noise. Joint stochastic-backprop reports retain relaxed objective/design choices and export metadata.

Per-layer min-max normalised probabilities and finite-bitstream noise are selected export semantics. Their source description does not establish unchanged trained-model accuracy after hardware conversion.
EP is documented as a research NumPy path; local adaptation/RTL handoff and stochastic-backprop parity exclude physical board measurement and timing/power qualification.

description: Expected outputs below are goals under construction.

expected_outputs.deliverable: Dataset/encoding/codec APIs with explicit timebase, loss and provenance, linked to independent stream tools.
expected_outputs.acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.

inputs: Whole classified parent source and existing consumers, explicit supported numerical/data/resource contracts; final per-component units and stable version matrix require owner freeze.

Selected files, labels, sensor geometry, source time units and published split are recorded with provenance. Real archives and deliberately selected synthetic fixtures are different input populations.
Timestep, observation window, polarity rule, dimensions, random seed and first-spike latency settings determine the tensor consumed by a network.

Binary rasters, event streams and electrode waveforms have different representations. Selected codecs require their dimensions/state; the waveform interface validates a finite nonempty time-by-channel matrix.
outputs: Dataset/encoding/codec APIs with explicit timebase, loss and provenance, linked to independent stream tools.

The dataset manifest binds file size/SHA, samples, labels/groups/splits and publisher metadata. Verification reports missing, altered and unlisted files; the manifest digest identifies the exact declared input.
The split plan binds its originating manifest and keeps complete groups on one side. Separate checks expose user-plan leakage and groups shared by the publisher’s original splits.
Frozen encoder declarations and digests retain exact binning/late-event/polarity/seed/latency rules; unknown schemas or changed rules are refused rather than reconstructed approximately.

Selected recorder rasters and codec bytes/results retain their specific read/shape/state contracts. A stored representation does not itself establish link timing, physical telemetry or empirical compression benefit.
acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
Current loader code and common contracts select synthetic generation only through the explicit flag; missing requested real data refuses. A test fixture is not the real corpus.
The documented poisson_encode path is one Bernoulli event per timestep, so it cannot emit multiple same-step events as a genuine Poisson count could.
SHD uses speaker groups; the event datasets identify recordings. Group checks do not invent an unavailable subject identity or a publisher train/test split for user-converted CIFAR data.
Header/input constraints and compression interfaces are source contracts; advertised ratios, Bluetooth feasibility and real-time latency need separate measured workload/device evidence.
partner_needs: Independent integrator for Dataset/encoding/codec APIs with explicit timebase, loss and provenance, linked to independent stream tools. expected_outputs.acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
expected_outputs.qualification_requirements: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.

inputs: Whole classified parent source and existing consumers, explicit supported numerical/data/resource contracts; final per-component units and stable version matrix require owner freeze.
Binary timestep trains, continuous spike times, trial populations, waveforms or field signals are different inputs. Each metric’s timestep/bin/window and units are declared.
Select metric, bins/lags/model order, surrogate null, trial/group population and any conditioning signals before interpreting a result.
GPFA receives binned population counts and explicit latent/bin/iteration settings; deterministic initialisation and the selected available backend define that estimator.
outputs: Observable definitions, analysis/plot APIs and provenance-preserving representations of scoped results.
Rate/interval/variability, spike-train distances, correlation and significance/pattern outputs report the selected observable rather than a universal neural-system score.
The documented EM contract returns trajectories, loading matrix, offset, diagonal noise and likelihood history; fixed timescales and consistent kernel jitter are retained estimator choices.
Selected Granger/VAR, PDC and DTF outputs retain their input validation, short-history and singular-frequency fallback conventions; the maintained dispatched path here is Python.

Phi* compares Gaussian past/future mutual information against contiguous bipartitions and returns a nonnegative reducibility estimate in nats. It is not a consciousness verdict or complete IIT partition search.
acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
GPFA reports measured absolute differences and conditional tests for built backends. Missing-backend skips and tight roundoff agreement do not establish universal or bit-exact parity.
The source explicitly keeps generated safety-note surfaces outside dispatched causality execution and owns the maintained estimator with Python/NumPy.
Selected callback/closure-based functions remain Rust-only or need Python wrappers. A module list cannot establish that every metric has the same PyO3 contract.
Small-window/coarse-grained Gaussian reducibility and contiguous partition comparison are diagnostic scope, not intrinsic causal power, consciousness or full IIT minimisation.

inputs: Whole classified parent source and existing consumers, explicit supported numerical/data/resource contracts; final per-component units and stable version matrix require owner freeze.

A validated EquationNeuron or supported NIR/SCNetwork graph supplies equations, committed state, weights, delays, thresholds and network structure. The selected integration method retains its own recurrence semantics.
Q-format widths, fractional bits, product rounding, overflow and LUT domains are selected contracts. Stochastic threshold sampling does not provide an implicit random source for product rounding.
Profile settings, work directory and actual external tools define the selected flow. Compiler metadata alone cannot establish a target’s physical behaviour.
outputs: Versioned IR/compiler API, generated Verilog/SystemVerilog and supported MLIR/CIRCT/formal/co-simulation collateral.

The source describes registered or folded Verilog, SC-NIR bundles, MLIR lowering and top-level assembly. These are distinct selected paths rather than a guarantee that every model completes every stage.
Precision planning, fixed-point lowering, formal/testbench and hardware numerical contracts retain their selected model and state/event scope. A LUT size is not a global accuracy percentage.
Synthesis/P&R/ASIC paths require actual tool results. Generated paths or source-line counts do not supply area, timing, power or energy evidence.
acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
The source lists multiple frontends, representations and external tools. Installed availability, supported model semantics and completed artefacts need exact per-flow evidence.
The compiler timing record comes from a loaded, unreserved workstation. The source expressly keeps it as local regression context and reports no maintained cross-language compiler timing comparison.
Independent packaging, migration and commercial boundaries remain separately decided. Parent implementation facts cannot become a standalone component release claim.

First fit: a genuine separately installed consumer of the agreed component contract, with missing/dependency/version-refusal and recovery evidence. description: Expected outputs below are goals under construction.

expected_outputs.deliverable: Target adapters, constraints/readout/driver interfaces and qualified target-specific deployment profiles.
expected_outputs.acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
expected_outputs.qualification_requirements: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.

inputs: Whole classified parent source and existing consumers, explicit supported numerical/data/resource contracts; final per-component units and stable version matrix require owner freeze.
The profile supplies identity, platform class, signed width/fraction, rounding/overflow and DSP constraints. Selection is configuration metadata with its own supported consumer path.
Supported compiler/HDL outputs, wrappers and driver contracts must match the selected model and target. A profile name does not resolve an arbitrary hardware instruction path.
Tool versions, constraints, physical flow and matching raw/report artefacts define what hardware claim can be made for the selected deployment.
outputs: Target adapters, constraints/readout/driver interfaces and qualified target-specific deployment profiles.
Public profile lookup/listing exposes the selected target’s metadata through the established compiler.platforms API without importing private registration internals.
The parent describes HDL assembly, target-oriented drivers and deployment/ASIC collateral. Their existence is separate from installing and exercising a genuine device consumer.
Matching synthesis/placement/timing/power and physical-device records support their own selected claims. Configuration/emulation cannot replace those records.
acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
The documented trap assertion is guarded by synthesis translate_off and stripped for synthesis. It does not become a runtime hardware protection mechanism merely because the profile selects trap.
Profiles describe target settings; emulators describe selected dynamics. Genuine installed target/driver/measurement paths still need their own evidence.
Source evidence organisation and formal collateral do not certify a device or convert generated line counts into timing/power/energy.
partner_needs: Independent integrator for Target adapters, constraints/readout/driver interfaces and qualified target-specific deployment profiles. First fit: a genuine separately installed consumer of the agreed component contract, with missing/dependency/version-refusal and recovery evidence. (architect proposal; no extraction or external commitment authorised)
open_fields: Group confirmation of reader synopsis and current public-source scope.
Exact source/runtime/physical qualification for the stated programme and consumer.
scope: Target profiles, mapping, deployment, drivers and power/thermal integration.

acceptance: Whole parent STABLE incl entire catalogue/Studio/retained components; reversible history/state/resource custody, installed genuine producer-consumer tests, missing-package recovery and complete component lifecycle gates.
A bounded proof covers its depth from reset. An unbounded result needs the appropriate invariant over every coupled state; UNKNOWN is inconclusive.
Shared free-product lifting is an opt-in over-approximation with a sound PASS argument in the described construction; FAIL can be spurious and does not automatically disprove the real design.
SHA seals detect content changes but are not signatures, recorder authentication or independent review. A receipt covers selected inputs/domain rather than arbitrary dependencies or operating points.
Bounded safety belongs to its own facet and cannot credit formal equivalence. Likewise state-field carriage does not establish numerical correctness or installed support.
Cycle obligations and structural CDC checks do not provide post-route nanoseconds or physical metastability resolution. Missing proof executables never count as a pass.
